proofs.proof_tex:
For a branch \(\alpha=(j,\omega)\in\Omega\), define
\[
 \mathsf{Succ}_{\alpha}(S,\ell,T,\tau)=1
\]
to mean that the following four statements hold: \(S\in\Pi\); the support table returned by \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}(S)\) assigns positive mass to \(H_{\mathrm{slice}}(S,\ell)\); \(T\) is a measured-ancestry single-district factor extracted from \(\operatorname{Slice}(S,\ell)\); and \(\tau\) is a valid successful \(\operatorname{IDENTIFY}^{+}\) ancestor--district transcript for the concrete assignment and equality type \(\omega\) of \(C_j\).  The source-slice, literal-encoding, and restriction-transcript definitions type these clauses.  Their support and ancestry requirements are exactly Assumptions \(\mathrm{Positive\ source\ law}\) and \(\mathrm{Measured\ ancestry}\).

Suppose first that the full correctly typed run
\[
 \operatorname{CTFIDU}^{+}(G,Q,\mathcal R(E_0))
\]
accepts.  By the target-factorization definition, its outer factor loop ranges over \(C_1,\ldots,C_k\).  By the definition of \(\Omega\), its finite concrete branch loop ranges over every \(\alpha=(j,\omega)\in\Omega\).  On each such branch the complete source search ranges over every decoded triple in \(\mathcal R(E_0)\).  Consequently,
\[
 \forall\alpha\in\Omega\quad
 \exists(S_{\alpha},\ell_{\alpha},T_{\alpha},\tau_{\alpha})
 \text{ represented in }E_0\quad
 \mathsf{Succ}_{\alpha}
 (S_{\alpha},\ell_{\alpha},T_{\alpha},\tau_{\alpha})=1.             \tag{1}
\]
Indeed, if (1) failed at \(\alpha\), the exhaustive source loop for that branch would exhaust \(\mathcal R(E_0)\) and return \(\operatorname{FAIL}\), contrary to acceptance.  This is the \(\forall\alpha\exists\) consequence of the complete run; no source has been selected uniformly over two branches.

Both \(\Omega\) and \(\mathcal R(E_0)\) are finite, so choose for each \(\alpha\) the lexicographically first witness in (1).  A successful call cannot have \(\mathfrak O(T_{\alpha},C_j)\ne\varnothing\), since Proposition \(\mathrm{Fixed\ factor\ obstruction}\) would then make that call return \(\operatorname{FAIL}\).  Hence \(\mathfrak O(T_{\alpha},C_j)=\varnothing\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{Fixed\ transcript\ size}\) replaces its trace, if necessary, by the canonical finite trace having at most \(|T_{\alpha}|\) strict restrictions, without changing success.

Partition \(\Omega\) by equality of the selected triple \((S_{\alpha},\ell_{\alpha},T_{\alpha})\).  For each nonempty cell make one switching record, let its branch-ownership mask be that cell, and attach the corresponding concrete transcript \(\tau_{\alpha}\) for every owned \(\alpha\).  The ownership masks are pairwise disjoint and their union is \(\Omega\), because every branch was assigned once.  There is at most one nonempty record per branch and therefore at most
\[
 |\Omega|=M=\sum_{j=1}^{k}|\Omega_j|                                      \tag{2}
\]
nonempty records and at most \(M\) distinct protocols.  Every record is well typed, positive, measured-ancestry compliant, and transcript-valid by (1).  It also follows from the construction that
\[
 \operatorname{Prot}(E_{\mathrm{sw}})
 \subseteq \operatorname{Prot}(E_0).                                      \tag{3}
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{Binary\ rational\ cost}\) gives \(c(a)\geq0\) for every action.  Thus the distinct-protocol cost definition and (3) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Cost}(E_{\mathrm{sw}})
 &=\sum_{S\in\operatorname{Prot}(E_{\mathrm{sw}})}\sum_{a\in S}c(a)\\
 &\leq\sum_{S\in\operatorname{Prot}(E_0)}\sum_{a\in S}c(a)
 =\operatorname{Cost}(E_0).                                                 \tag{4}
 \end{aligned}
\]

It remains to check the complete-run clause rather than merely the claimed transcripts.  Fix \(\alpha\).  Its owner contributes its successful triple to \(\mathcal R(E_{\mathrm{sw}})\), so the exhaustive source loop for \(\alpha\) encounters a successful \(\operatorname{IDENTIFY}^{+}\) call.  This holds for every \(\alpha\in\Omega\); hence every concrete branch of every structural factor succeeds and the complete unconditional run on \(\mathcal R(E_{\mathrm{sw}})\) does not return \(\operatorname{FAIL}\).  All rejection conditions in the definition of switching operational acceptance have already been excluded, so
\[
 \operatorname{Acc}_{\mathrm{sw}}(Q,E_{\mathrm{sw}};G)=1.                    \tag{5}
\]

Conversely, suppose \(\operatorname{Acc}_{\mathrm{sw}}(Q,E_{\mathrm{sw}};G)=1\).  By the definition of switching operational acceptance, the verifier constructs the entire deduplicated collection \(\mathcal R(E_{\mathrm{sw}})\) from the nonempty records and executes the complete unconditional procedure on that collection.  Acceptance expressly requires that this run not return \(\operatorname{FAIL}\).  Therefore \(E_{\mathrm{sw}}\) induces a complete accepting \(\operatorname{CTFIDU}^{+}\) run on \(\mathcal R(E_{\mathrm{sw}})\).  Equivalently, its partition of \(\Omega\) witnesses exactly
\[
 \forall(j,\omega)\in\Omega\;\exists(S,\ell,T,\tau)\quad
 \mathsf{Succ}_{(j,\omega)}(S,\ell,T,\tau)=1,
\]
and the proof nowhere exchanges these quantifiers.

Assume that the independently specified oracle-instance is feasible.  Lemma \(\mathrm{Canonical\ certificate\ bound}\) then supplies an accepted canonical switching certificate whose exact length is at most \(B_{\mathrm{sw}}\) and whose cost is no larger than the cost of any accepting acquired collection.  In particular, the infimum in the definition of \(\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}\) equals the minimum cost among accepted canonical strings of length at most \(B_{\mathrm{sw}}\).

Enumerate all binary strings of lengths \(0,1,\ldots,B_{\mathrm{sw}}\) in canonical lexicographic order.  Their number is
\[
 \sum_{r=0}^{B_{\mathrm{sw}}}2^r
 =2^{B_{\mathrm{sw}}+1}-1.                                                   \tag{12}
\]
For each string apply the total parser in the definition of switching operational acceptance.  Malformed strings are rejected.  For a parsed candidate, check that its nonempty ownership masks partition the explicitly indexed \(M\) branches; check protocol legality and all catalogue values; query the source interface; use its exact support table to check that every asserted conditioning event has positive mass; verify source extraction and measured ancestry; and verify every concrete ancestor--district transcript.  Construct the complete deduplicated collection \(\mathcal R(E_{\mathrm{sw}})\) and execute the required full unconditional \(\operatorname{CTFIDU}^{+}\) run.  These are exactly the acceptance clauses, so this test accepts exactly the strings \(E_{\mathrm{sw}}\) for which \(\operatorname{Acc}_{\mathrm{sw}}(Q,E_{\mathrm{sw}};G)=1\).

Cache \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}(S)\) under the \(|\mathcal A|\)-bit mask \(S\) for the whole enumeration.  Thus each distinct queried protocol produces one charged reply, and every query bit, returned handle bit, support-index bit, and support-table bit is included in \(N_{\mathcal O}\), as required by the physical-input definition.  Graph traversals, mask operations, support lookups, and transcript checks are polynomial in \(N_{\mathrm{in}}+B_{\mathrm{sw}}+N_{\mathcal O}\).  The complete finite run ranges over decoded sources, target branches, vertex subsets generated by its recursion, and value comparisons, all encoded within the structural input and the candidate of length at most \(B_{\mathrm{sw}}\); its work is bounded by \(2^{O(B_{\mathrm{sw}})}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})\).  Combining this with (12) gives total time
\[
 2^{O(B_{\mathrm{sw}})}
 \operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+B_{\mathrm{sw}}+N_{\mathcal O}).       \tag{13}
\]

For every accepted string compute, by the distinct-protocol cost definition,
\[
 \operatorname{Cost}(E_{\mathrm{sw}})
 =\sum_{S\in\operatorname{Prot}(E_{\mathrm{sw}})}\sum_{a\in S}c(a).         \tag{14}
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{Binary\ rational\ cost}\) permits exact comparison of these finite nonnegative rational sums.  Retain the least value and, on a tie, the lexicographically first canonical string.  Lemma \(\mathrm{Canonical\ certificate\ bound}\) proves that no longer switching certificate and no accepting generic acquisition has smaller cost.  Therefore the retained certificate is \(E_{\mathrm{sw}}^{\star}\), (14) equals \(\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}\), and its length obeys \(N_{E_{\mathrm{sw}}^{\star}}\leq B_{\mathrm{sw}}\).  Decoding its fixed-width fields and self-delimiting tails outputs precisely its protocol masks, \(|\mathrm{LIT}|\)-bit slice labels, source masks, \(M\)-bit branch-ownership masks, and one finite concrete transcript for every owned branch.  This proves attainment, the output guarantee, and (13), without asserting a polynomial bound on \(B_{\mathrm{sw}}\).

Let
\[
 \mathcal F_{\mathrm{sw}}
 =\{E_{\mathrm{sw}}:\operatorname{Acc}_{\mathrm{sw}}(Q,E_{\mathrm{sw}};G)=1\}.
\]
If \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{sw}}\ne\varnothing\), Theorem \(\mathrm{Cost\text{-}optimal\ certificate\ feasibility}\) returns \(E_{\mathrm{sw}}^{\star}\), and
\[
 \operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}
 =\operatorname{Cost}(E_{\mathrm{sw}}^{\star})<+\infty.                     \tag{15}
\]
If \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{sw}}=\varnothing\), the empty-family convention in the definition of switching optimal cost gives
\[
 \operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}=\inf\varnothing=+\infty.                 \tag{16}
\]
These two cases are disjoint and exhaustive, proving the first alternative.

Lemma \(\mathrm{Canonical\ certificate\ bound}\) gives
\[
 \mathcal F_{\mathrm{sw}}\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \exists E_{\mathrm{sw}}\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{sw}}
 \text{ with }N_{\mathrm{sw}}\leq B_{\mathrm{sw}}.                          \tag{17}
\]
The forward implication is the lemma's canonicalization conclusion and the reverse implication is immediate.  Theorem \(\mathrm{Switching\ source\ normal\ form}\) gives independently
\[
 \mathcal F_{\mathrm{sw}}\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \exists E_0\text{ finite and correctly typed such that }
 \operatorname{CTFIDU}^{+}(G,Q,\mathcal R(E_0))\text{ accepts}.              \tag{18}
\]
Its forward direction is the theorem's converse clause; its reverse direction is its switching construction.  Negating (17) and (18) proves both asserted characterizations of infeasibility.

Finally, enumerate all strings of length at most \(B_{\mathrm{sw}}\) and test switching operational acceptance exactly as in Theorem \(\mathrm{Cost\text{-}optimal\ certificate\ feasibility}\), caching one oracle reply for every queried distinct protocol.  That theorem's analysis gives time
\[
 2^{O(B_{\mathrm{sw}})}
 \operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+B_{\mathrm{sw}}+N_{\mathcal O}).       \tag{19}
\]
By (17), rejection of every enumerated string is equivalent to \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{sw}}=\varnothing\), and then (16) and (18) give the two claimed negative certificates.  In this case the procedure returns only the decision and does not encode an output switching certificate, so no certificate-output-length term is required.

theorem.statement:
Let \(m=|\mathcal A|\) and \(L=|\mathrm{LIT}|\).  Exact minimum-cost optimization over uniform certificates accepted by \(\operatorname{Acc}\) has a deterministic algorithm using at most \(2^m\) distinct queries to \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}\), time
\[
 2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O}),
\]
and oracle-answer space \(2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})\).  It returns the lexicographically first optimum uniform certificate when \(\operatorname{Opt}<+\infty\), and otherwise certifies \(\operatorname{Opt}=+\infty\).  Thus the algorithmic alternative in the oracle-search question holds; no subexponential oracle lower bound or compact scalar identifying functional is asserted.
theorem.proof_tex:
Put \(m=|\mathcal A|\), \(L=|\mathrm{LIT}|\), and \(n=|V|\).  We give an explicit finite algorithm and prove that it optimizes the observed source-certificate functional \(\operatorname{Opt}\); no equality with a scalar evaluation of the causal joint \(Q\) is used.

First enumerate the \(2^m\) protocol masks in canonical order.  Membership in \(\Pi\) is decided from the explicit action record by counting SELECT actions and checking freshness, the at-most-once mechanism rule, precedence closure, conflicts, allowed values, and physical compatibility.  All checks except physical compatibility are direct scans of the encoded relations.  Lemma \(\mathrm{Published\ CTF\text{-}REALIZE\ runtime}\) makes the remaining CTF-REALIZE test polynomial in the finite graph and protocol encodings.  Query \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}\) once for each legal mask and cache the reply.  There are therefore at most \(2^m\) distinct oracle queries.  A reply equal to \(\bot\), or one with a malformed support index, yields no source candidate.

For each remaining \(S\), enumerate the \(2^L\) literal masks \(\ell\).  The literal table decides consistency and catalogue membership, while the returned exact support table decides whether \(H_{\mathrm{slice}}(S,\ell)\) has positive mass.  Only positive events define \(\operatorname{Slice}(S,\ell)\), by the measured source-slice definition and Assumption \(\mathrm{Positive\ source\ law}\).  Apply the encoded ancestral-set transformation and bidirected-district factorization to that slice.  There are at most \(n\) resulting single-district factors.  Retain exactly those factors that pass Assumption \(\mathrm{Measured\ ancestry}\).

Fix a retained triple \((S,\ell,T)\) and a target factor \(C_j\).  Enumerate every \(\omega\in\Omega_j\).  If the free request positions have domain sizes \(q_1,\ldots,q_r\), their assignment determines its equality type, and
\[
 |\Omega_j|=\prod_{h=1}^{r}q_h
 \leq 2^{\sum_{h=1}^{r}q_h}
 \leq 2^L.                                                                  \tag{6}
\]
The first inequality uses \(q\leq2^q\) for every positive integer \(q\); the second uses the distinct request literal present for each of the \(q_h\) allowed values.  For each branch, instantiate all value comparisons, construct \(D_T\), and execute the deterministic ancestor--district recursion.  Proposition \(\mathrm{Fixed\ factor\ obstruction}\) decides whether the call succeeds, and Lemma \(\mathrm{Fixed\ transcript\ size}\) constructs its canonical finite transcript when it does.  Since each ancestor set and retained district is determined by the instantiated graph, the canonical traces also decide whether one encoded transcript schema verifies for every \(\omega\in\Omega_j\).  Thus exhaustive comparison of the canonical traces decides, soundly and completely, whether \((S,\ell,T)\) is a uniform witness for \(C_j\).

For a protocol \(S\), define the computable set
\[
 K(S)=\{j\in[k]:\text{some enumerated }(\ell,T,\tau_j)
       \text{ is a uniform witness for }C_j\}.                               \tag{7}
\]
Retain all canonical witness records, ordered lexicographically.  The uniform-certificate and operational-acceptance definitions give the exact equivalence
\[
 \exists E\;\operatorname{Acc}(Q,E;G)=1
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \exists\mathcal P\subseteq\Pi\quad
 \bigcup_{S\in\mathcal P}K(S)=[k].                                          \tag{8}
\]
For the forward implication, the unique owner of each factor in an accepted certificate supplies a uniform witness counted in \(K(S)\) for its record's protocol.  For the reverse implication, assign every \(j\) to a selected protocol covering it, choose an enumerated witness, merge factors having the same protocol--slice--source record, and sort the records.  The resulting ownership masks partition \([k]\); positivity, source typing, and every cross-branch transcript check hold by construction.  For every concrete branch the complete source search encounters its retained successful record, so the complete run also succeeds and \(\operatorname{Acc}(Q,E;G)=1\).

Write \(w(S)=\sum_{a\in S}c(a)\).  Because the certificate cost charges each distinct protocol once, (8) proves the optimization identity
\[
 \operatorname{Opt}
 =\min_{\mathcal P\subseteq\Pi:\,\cup_{S\in\mathcal P}K(S)=[k]}
   \sum_{S\in\mathcal P}w(S),                                               \tag{9}
\]
where the minimum over an empty feasible family is \(+\infty\).  Equation (9) is derived from acceptance and the cost definition; it does not redefine the causal target \(Q\).

List the candidate protocols as \(S_1,\ldots,S_p\), where \(p\leq2^m\).  For \(U\subseteq[k]\), let \(D_0(\varnothing)=0\), let \(D_0(U)=+\infty\) for \(U\ne\varnothing\), and set
\[
 D_i(U)=\min\{D_{i-1}(U),\;D_{i-1}(U\setminus K(S_i))+w(S_i)\}.              \tag{10}
\]
Induction on \(i\) proves that \(D_i(U)\) is the minimum cost of a subcollection of \(S_1,\ldots,S_i\) covering \(U\): an optimum either omits \(S_i\), which gives the first term, or includes it, after which the earlier protocols need cover only \(U\setminus K(S_i)\).  Hence \(D_p([k])\) equals (9).  Binary-rational arithmetic is exact by Assumption \(\mathrm{Binary\ rational\ cost}\).

To recover the lexicographically first optimum certificate rather than merely its value, apply standard finite self-reduction to this same recurrence: scan the bits of the canonical certificate encoding from left to right, tentatively set the next bit to zero, and retain that choice exactly when the constrained version of (10), together with the enumerated witness table, still admits cost \(D_p([k])\); otherwise set it to one.  Factor ownership is unique, and the available records and their canonical transcripts are explicit and finite, so each constrained feasibility test is another set-cover recurrence on the same \(p\) protocol rows and \(2^k\) factor states.  After at most the canonical uniform-certificate encoding length many tests, this yields exactly the lexicographically first optimum accepted certificate.

Finally, because every \(C_j\) is nonempty, its request-literal block contains at least one literal and the blocks have distinct first coordinates.  Therefore \(k\leq L\).  Candidate generation makes at most
\[
 2^m\,2^L\,n k\,2^L
 =2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}})                              \tag{11}
\]
local branch checks, and (10) makes at most \(p2^k\leq2^{m+L}\) updates per self-reduction test.  The number of self-reduction tests and every transcript length are polynomial in the explicit input and in \(m+L\), by Lemma \(\mathrm{Fixed\ transcript\ size}\).  Every support bit read is included in \(N_{\mathcal O}\); caching uses \(O(N_{\mathcal O})\) bits.  The candidate table, canonical witnesses, and dynamic-program layers use \(2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})\) space.  Together with (11), this proves the stated query, time, and space bounds.  If (10) is infinite, (8) certifies \(\operatorname{Opt}=+\infty\); otherwise the self-reduction returns the asserted optimum certificate.
theorem.justification: The theorem resolves the oracle frontier constructively by reducing exact uniform-certificate acquisition to finite protocol enumeration followed by an explicit weighted factor-cover dynamic program.
theorem.gap: The unrestricted source interface has no useful local-width representation, but its finite protocol-mask universe still permits an exact singly exponential algorithm in the action and literal tables.
theorem.consumer: The restricted uniform-certificate planner can return an exact least-cost certificate or a finite infeasibility decision while charging all source-oracle traffic.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix an instance \((G^{+},\mathcal A,Q)\in\mathfrak C_{1}\).  Because \(\mathcal A\) is finite, \(2^{\mathcal A}\), and hence the legal-protocol class \(\Pi\subseteq 2^{\mathcal A}\) of Definition \(\text{def:legal-protocols}\), is finite.  For \(S\in\Pi\), set
\[
 w(S):=\sum_{a\in S}c(a).
\]
Assumption \(\text{ass:binary-rational-cost}\) gives \(w(S)\in\mathbb Q_{\geq 0}\).  Assumption \(\text{ass:single-paid-action}\) says that there is exactly one \(a_S\in S\) with \(c(a_S)>0\), and therefore \(w(S)=c(a_S)\).  Distinct protocol masks are nevertheless distinct cover objects even if their unique paid actions coincide: Definition \(\text{def:certificate-cost}\) charges each distinct acquired protocol once.

For \(S\in\Pi\), use the factor set in the statement,
\[
 U(S)=\{j\in[k]: C_j\text{ has an individually valid uniform certificate record using }S\}.
\]
Spelling out ``individually valid'' using Definitions \(\text{def:acquisition-certificate}\) and \(\text{def:operational-acceptance}\), membership \(j\in U(S)\) supplies a fixed literal label \(\ell\), a labelled source factor \(T\) extracted from the returned law for \(S\), and a transcript \(\tau_j\) such that the singleton-ownership record
\[
 R_{S,j}=(b_S,b_{\ell},b_{\{j\}},b_T,\tau_j)
\]
passes all catalogue, legality, and typing checks and succeeds for every branch in \(\Omega_j\).  In particular, the oracle reply is not \(\bot\), the event \(H_{\mathrm{slice}}(S,\ell)\) is defined and has strictly positive support, every retained ancestor is measured in the source, and the same \((S,\ell,T,\tau_j)\) works throughout \(\Omega_j\).  Thus no zero-probability conditional law or assignment-dependent source switch is hidden in \(U(S)\).  Positivity is used only to make the displayed source slice well typed.  No rank condition, matrix inversion, overlap ratio, or limiting argument is used below.

We first map accepted certificates to covers.  Let \(E\) satisfy \(\operatorname{Acc}(Q,E;G)=1\), and write \(\mathcal P(E)=\operatorname{Prot}(E)\).  By Definitions \(\text{def:acquisition-certificate}\) and \(\text{def:operational-acceptance}\), after empty ownership masks are discarded, the ownership masks of the records of \(E\) partition \([k]\).  Hence every \(j\in[k]\) has a unique owning record, using some protocol \(S_j\in\mathcal P(E)\), whose fixed slice, source, and transcript are valid uniformly over \(\Omega_j\).  That record witnesses \(j\in U(S_j)\).  Consequently
\[
 [k]=\bigcup_{S\in\mathcal P(E)}U(S).
\tag{1}
\]
Thus \(\mathcal P(E)\) is a set cover.  The distinct-protocol convention in Definition \(\text{def:certificate-cost}\) gives, without double charging protocols used by several records,
\[
 \operatorname{Cost}(E)
 =\sum_{S\in\mathcal P(E)}\sum_{a\in S}c(a)
 =\sum_{S\in\mathcal P(E)}w(S).
\tag{2}
\]

Conversely, let \(\mathcal P\subseteq\Pi\) satisfy
\[
 \bigcup_{S\in\mathcal P}U(S)=[k].
\tag{3}
\]
For each \(j\in[k]\), choose \(s(j)\in\mathcal P\) with \(j\in U(s(j))\), together with one witnessing label, source, and uniform transcript.  Form the singleton-ownership record for each \(j\), and let
\[
 \mathcal P':=\{s(j):j\in[k]\}\subseteq\mathcal P.
\]
Every chosen record has a legal protocol, an in-catalogue consistent label, a defined positive-support slice, a measured-ancestry source factor, and a transcript valid for every branch of its owned factor.  Its ownership mask is \(\{j\}\), so the ownership masks partition \([k]\).  Assumption \(\text{ass:protocolwise-legality}\) ensures that acquiring the protocols in \(\mathcal P'\) on distinct fresh units preserves the legality of every constituent protocol.  Assumption \(\text{ass:factorwise-no-synergy}\) ensures that the individual certification of \(C_j\) by its selected protocol is unaffected by adjoining the other acquired protocols.  Therefore the complete exhaustive run required by Definition \(\text{def:operational-acceptance}\) encounters the displayed successful source for every target factor and does not return \(\operatorname{FAIL}\).  The resulting certificate \(E(\mathcal P)\) obeys
\[
 \operatorname{Acc}(Q,E(\mathcal P);G)=1.
\tag{4}
\]
By Definition \(\text{def:certificate-cost}\) and nonnegativity of \(w\),
\[
 \operatorname{Cost}(E(\mathcal P))
 =\sum_{S\in\mathcal P'}w(S)
 \leq \sum_{S\in\mathcal P}w(S).
\tag{5}
\]

Since \(\Pi\) is finite, a feasible cover family has a minimum-cost member.  Starting from one and deleting redundant protocols terminates at an inclusion-minimal minimum-cost cover \(\mathcal P^{\star}\); deletion cannot increase cost because all weights are nonnegative, and it cannot lower the cost below the minimum.  For each \(S\in\mathcal P^{\star}\), inclusion minimality supplies a private factor
\[
 j_S\in U(S)\setminus
 \bigcup_{S'\in\mathcal P^{\star}\setminus\{S\}}U(S').
\tag{6}
\]
In the construction above, assign \(j_S\) to \(S\) and assign every other factor to an arbitrary protocol of \(\mathcal P^{\star}\) covering it.  Equation (6) forces every \(S\in\mathcal P^{\star}\) to occur in the image of \(s\); hence \(\mathcal P'=\mathcal P^{\star}\), and equality holds in (5).  Equations (1)--(5) and Definition \(\text{def:optimal-cost}\) now yield
\[
 \operatorname{Opt}
 =\min_{\mathcal P\subseteq\Pi:\,\bigcup_{S\in\mathcal P}U(S)=[k]}
   \sum_{S\in\mathcal P}w(S).
\tag{7}
\]
At the infeasible boundary, the family on the right of (7) is empty.  Then (1) rules out an accepted certificate, so both sides are \(+\infty\) under the convention in Definition \(\text{def:optimal-cost}\).

Assume next that \(\operatorname{Opt}<+\infty\).  We apply the standard weighted greedy rule named in Lemma \(\text{lem:published-weighted-greedy-approximation}\), and derive its precise \(H_k\) guarantee for the present finite cover.  First select every zero-weight protocol and put
\[
 R_0=[k]\setminus\bigcup_{S:\,w(S)=0}U(S).
\]
This preprocessing costs zero.  While \(R_{i-1}\neq\varnothing\), choose an eligible \(S_i\in\Pi\) minimizing
\[
 \frac{w(S)}{|U(S)\cap R_{i-1}|}
\tag{8}
\]
among protocols satisfying \(U(S)\cap R_{i-1}\neq\varnothing\), and set
\[
 R_i=R_{i-1}\setminus U(S_i).
\]
Feasibility in (7) makes the eligible family nonempty whenever \(R_{i-1}\neq\varnothing\), and finiteness of \(\Pi\) makes the minimum attainable.  Every zero-weight protocol covers no element of \(R_0\); hence every protocol eligible in (8) has positive numerator, while eligibility gives a positive integer denominator.  Thus every division in (8) is defined.  At least one factor is removed per iteration, so the procedure stops after at most \(k\) iterations.

Let \(r_i=|U(S_i)\cap R_{i-1}|\), and charge each factor first covered at iteration \(i\) the amount
\[
 \rho_j=\frac{w(S_i)}{r_i}.
\]
The newly covered factor sets are disjoint and have cardinalities \(r_i\), so
\[
 \sum_i w(S_i)=\sum_{j\in R_0}\rho_j.
\tag{9}
\]
Fix \(S\in\mathcal P^{\star}\), where \(\mathcal P^{\star}\) is a minimum cover in (7), and order the \(m=|U(S)\cap R_0|\) relevant factors as \(j_1,\ldots,j_m\) by the iterations at which greedy first covers them, resolving simultaneous ties arbitrarily.  Immediately before \(j_q\) is covered, at least \(m-q+1\) members of \(U(S)\cap R_0\) remain.  Thus \(S\) is eligible in (8) with denominator at least \(m-q+1\).  Greedy minimality gives
\[
 \rho_{j_q}\leq \frac{w(S)}{m-q+1}.
\]
Summing, using \(m\leq k\), and writing \(H_k=\sum_{r=1}^{k}r^{-1}\), gives
\[
 \sum_{j\in U(S)\cap R_0}\rho_j
 \leq w(S)\sum_{q=1}^{m}\frac{1}{m-q+1}
 =w(S)H_m
 \leq w(S)H_k.
\tag{10}
\]
If \(w(S)=0\), then \(U(S)\cap R_0=\varnothing\), so (10) remains valid with both sides zero.  Since \(\mathcal P^{\star}\) covers \([k]\), every \(j\in R_0\) belongs to at least one of the sets summed on the left of (10).  Charges are nonnegative; therefore (7), (9), and (10) imply
\[
 \sum_i w(S_i)
 =\sum_{j\in R_0}\rho_j
 \leq\sum_{S\in\mathcal P^{\star}}
       \sum_{j\in U(S)\cap R_0}\rho_j
 \leq H_k\sum_{S\in\mathcal P^{\star}}w(S)
 =H_k\operatorname{Opt}.
\tag{11}
\]
The zero-weight protocols together with the \(S_i\) cover \([k]\).  Applying the cover-to-certificate construction of (3)--(5), and omitting selected zero-weight protocols to which no factor was assigned, produces an accepted legal certificate \(E_{\mathrm{gr}}\) with
\[
 \operatorname{Cost}(E_{\mathrm{gr}})
 \leq\sum_i w(S_i)
 \leq H_k\operatorname{Opt}.
\]

For an exact smallest nontrivial check, take \(k=2\) and three independently legal protocols, each with one paid action, whose factor sets are \(\{1,2\}\), \(\{1\}\), and \(\{2\}\), and whose weights are \(2,1,1\), respectively.  The cover optimum and every greedy outcome both have cost \(2\), in agreement with (7) and (11).  The no-synergy condition is load-bearing for the reduction: if \(U(S_1)=U(S_2)=\varnothing\) but the two-source collection jointly certifies the target factors, an accepted acquisition exists although the induced cover instance is infeasible.  Protocolwise legality is also load-bearing: if \(U(S_1)=\{1\}\) and \(U(S_2)=\{2\}\) but acquiring the pair is forbidden, the cover is feasible although the corresponding combined certificate is not.  These finite witnesses explain the stated restriction to \(\mathfrak C_1\).

For \(m\in\{1,2\}\), let \(Y_x^{(m)}\) and \(Z_x^{(m)}\) denote the potential responses obtained by replacing the occurrence of \(X\) in the structural equation of model \(M_m\) by \(x\).  The equations in Definition \(\mathrm{Positive\ binary\ separation\ models\ and\ catalogue}\) give the complete table
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc|cc}
 &Y_0^{(m)}&Z_0^{(m)}&Y_1^{(m)}&Z_1^{(m)}\\ \hline
m=1&U_A\mathbin\oplus E_Y&U_B\mathbin\oplus E_Z&U_B\mathbin\oplus E_Y&U_C\mathbin\oplus E_Z\\
m=2&U_A\mathbin\oplus E_Y&U_B\mathbin\oplus E_Z&U_C\mathbin\oplus E_Y&U_A\mathbin\oplus E_Z.
\end{array}
\tag{1}
\]
The same definition states that \(U_X,U_A,U_B,U_C\) are mutually independent fair bits, that \(E_Y,E_Z\) are mutually independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\varepsilon)\) bits, and that the two groups are independent.  For each \(m\in\{1,2\}\) and \(x\in\{0,1\}\), the two pre-noise bits occurring in \((Y_x^{(m)},Z_x^{(m)})\) in (1) are therefore distinct independent fair bits.  If \(B\) is a fair bit independent of a bit \(E\), then, for each \(b\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 \Pr(B\mathbin\oplus E=b)
 =\sum_{e=0}^1\Pr(E=e)\Pr(B=b\mathbin\oplus e)
 =\frac12\sum_{e=0}^1\Pr(E=e)=\frac12.
\tag{2}
\]
Applying (2) coordinatewise and using the independence of the two pre-noise bits and the two noise bits yields
\[
 \Pr_{M_m}\!\left(Y_x^{(m)}=y,Z_x^{(m)}=z\right)=\frac14
 \quad
 (m\in\{1,2\},\ x,y,z\in\{0,1\}).
\tag{3}
\]

We verify all ordinary regimes directly.  Fix
\(r=(r_X,r_Y,r_Z)\in\{\mathrm{natural},0,1\}^{\{X,Y,Z\}}\), and let \(P_{m,r}\) be the law in model \(M_m\) after replacing the structural equation of every coordinate \(W\) for which \(r_W\in\{0,1\}\) by the constant \(r_W\).  Because \(Y\) and \(Z\) are sinks, intervention on either one does not change any other structural equation.  If \(X\) is fixed to \(x\), (3) says that the unfixed members of \(\{Y,Z\}\) are independent fair bits.  If \(X\) is natural, then \(X=U_X\); conditional on \(X=x\), the same conclusion follows from (3), and that conditional law is independent of \(x\).  Moreover, \(U_X\) is fair and independent of every response and noise bit.  Marginalizing any intervened sink from these joint laws shows that all natural coordinates under \(P_{m,r}\) are mutually independent fair bits, whereas every fixed coordinate equals its assigned value.  Consequently, for every \(a=(a_X,a_Y,a_Z)\in\{0,1\}^3\),
\[
 P_{m,r}(a)
 =\prod_{W:\,r_W\ne\mathrm{natural}}\mathbf 1\{a_W=r_W\}
  \prod_{W:\,r_W=\mathrm{natural}}\frac12,
 \qquad m\in\{1,2\}.
\tag{4}
\]
There are \(3^3=27\) choices of \(r\), so (4) proves equality of the two models under every ordinary observational or simultaneous node-interventional regime asserted in the proposition.

Both structural systems are recursive in the order \(X\) before \(Y,Z\).  Their displayed response functions admit \(X\) as a directed parent of both \(Y\) and \(Z\).  In \(M_1\), the exogenous bit \(U_B\) is an argument of both response functions, and in \(M_2\), the exogenous bit \(U_A\) is an argument of both response functions; this shared exogenous input is represented by \(Y\leftrightarrow Z\).  No response exogenous variable is shared with \(X\).  Thus both models are compatible with the ADMG containing \(X\to Y\), \(X\to Z\), and \(Y\leftrightarrow Z\).

At \(\varepsilon=1/10\), every atom of the six exogenous bits has strictly positive probability.  Formula (4) also shows that every assignment of the nonintervened variables in every ordinary regime has positive probability.  The edge-specific source laws used below are positive as well.  When their two response coordinates use distinct fair bits, all four cells have probability \(1/4\).  When they share a fair bit \(B\), the probability of either diagonal cell is
\[
 \frac12\bigl((1-\varepsilon)^2+\varepsilon^2\bigr)>0,
\]
and the probability of either off-diagonal cell is \(\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)>0\), since \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\).  Hence all conditioning and READ cells used below lie in the returned support.

The cross-world probabilities differ.  By (1), \(Y_0^{(1)}\) is a function only of \((U_A,E_Y)\), whereas \(Z_1^{(1)}\) is a function only of \((U_C,E_Z)\).  These pairs are independent, and (2) makes both responses fair.  Therefore
\[
 \Pr_{M_1}(Y_0=1,Z_1=1)=\frac12\cdot\frac12=\frac14.
\tag{5}
\]
In \(M_2\), both responses use \(U_A\).  Conditioning on that fair bit and using independence of \(E_Y,E_Z\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Pr_{M_2}(Y_0=1,Z_1=1)
 &=\Pr(U_A=1,E_Y=0,E_Z=0)
   +\Pr(U_A=0,E_Y=1,E_Z=1)\\
 &=\frac12(1-\varepsilon)^2+\frac12\varepsilon^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
Substitution of \(\varepsilon=1/10\) into (6) gives
\[
 \frac12\left(\frac9{10}\right)^2+
 \frac12\left(\frac1{10}\right)^2
 =\frac{41}{100}.
\tag{7}
\]

It remains to verify the physical acquisitions.  Under \(S_{\mathrm{ind}}\), the edge-specific action \(\chi_{Y,0}\) replaces the value transmitted from \(X\) to the mechanism for \(Y\) by zero and leaves the transmission to \(Z\) natural.  The acquired variables consequently satisfy
\[
 X^{\mathrm{ind}}=U_X,
 \qquad Y^{\mathrm{ind}}=Y_0,
 \qquad Z^{\mathrm{ind}}=Z_{U_X}.
\tag{8}
\]
The event \(X^{\mathrm{ind}}=1\) has probability \(1/2>0\).  Because \(U_X\) is independent of every variable entering \((Y_0,Z_1)\), (8) implies, in either model,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\Pr\!\left(Y^{\mathrm{ind}}=1,Z^{\mathrm{ind}}=1
       \mid X^{\mathrm{ind}}=1,S_{\mathrm{ind}}\right)\\
 &\qquad=\Pr(Y_0=1,Z_1=1\mid U_X=1)
 =\Pr(Y_0=1,Z_1=1).
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]
By Definition \(\mathrm{Acquired\ regime}\), the source oracle returns and caches the complete law and exact support table of this displayed protocol.  The positivity just proved and Definition \(\mathrm{Measured\ source\ slice}\) imply that the READ projection conditioned on \(X=1\) is a defined source slice.  Its \((Y,Z)=(1,1)\) cell is the left side of (9), and hence identifies the stated joint within each displayed SCM.

Under \(S_{\mathrm{dir}}\), the two edge-specific actions transmit zero to the \(Y\)-mechanism and one to the \(Z\)-mechanism.  Therefore
\[
 Y^{\mathrm{dir}}=Y_0,
 \qquad Z^{\mathrm{dir}}=Z_1,
\tag{10}
\]
so the unconditioned READ law directly exposes the same joint.

We finally check protocol legality and cost.  Each displayed protocol contains exactly the one fresh-iid SELECT action \(s\).  Each listed edge mechanism and each READ mechanism occurs at most once.  The catalogue order places \(s\) before every included CTF-RAND action and those actions before the included READs, and the catalogue has no conflicts.  The executions in (8) and (10) simultaneously assign only the indicated child-specific transmissions on one selected unit, furnishing the required CTF-REALIZE compatibility witness on \(G^+\).  Definition \(\mathrm{Legal\ protocol\ class}\) thus gives
\[
 S_{\mathrm{ind}},S_{\mathrm{dir}}\in\Pi(G^+,\mathcal A_{\mathrm{sep}}).
\tag{11}
\]
To keep the cost calculation well typed, let \(F_{\mathrm{ind}}\) be the acquired collection containing the positive slice in (9), and let \(F_{\mathrm{dir}}\) be the acquired collection containing the unconditioned source in (10).  Their distinct-protocol sets are respectively \(\{S_{\mathrm{ind}}\}\) and \(\{S_{\mathrm{dir}}\}\).  Definition \(\mathrm{Distinct\text{-}protocol\ cost}\) and the catalogue costs therefore give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Cost}(F_{\mathrm{ind}})
 &=c_{\mathrm{sep}}(\chi_{Y,0})=1,\\
 \operatorname{Cost}(F_{\mathrm{dir}})
 &=c_{\mathrm{sep}}(\chi_{Y,0})+c_{\mathrm{sep}}(\chi_{Z,1})=2,
\end{aligned}
\tag{12}
\]
because \(s,\rho_X,\rho_Y,\rho_Z\) have zero cost.  Since further slices of an already acquired protocol are free by that same definition, (12) is precisely the asserted cost-one versus cost-two protocol comparison.  Equations (4)--(12) establish every claim of the proposition.

Put \(m=|\mathcal A|\), \(L=|\mathrm{LIT}|\), and \(n=|V|\).  We give a finite algorithm, prove that its feasible objects are exactly the certificates accepted by \(\operatorname{Acc}\), and then bound its resources.

First enumerate the \(2^m\) protocol masks \(S\) in canonical order.  Membership in \(\Pi\) is decidable from Definition~\(\mathrm{Legal\ protocol\ class}\): count the SELECT actions, check the fresh-unit flag, the at-most-once mechanism condition, every precedence and conflict relation in the explicit catalogue, and CTF-REALIZE compatibility on \(G^{+}\).  All checks except the last are scans of the finite structural input.  The published CTF-REALIZE runtime lemma makes the last check polynomial in the encoded protocol and graph.  Query \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}\) once for each legal mask and cache its immutable answer.  Thus no more than \(2^m\) distinct oracle queries are made.  A reply equal to \(\bot\), or a reply whose self-delimiting support index does not have the format in Definition~\(\mathrm{Certificate\mbox{-}independent\ physical\ input}\), supplies no candidate slice.

For each remaining protocol, enumerate the \(2^L\) masks \(\ell\).  Definition~\(\mathrm{Canonical\ literal\ and\ label\ encoding}\) decides by a finite scan whether \(\ell\) is consistent and uses only catalogued values.  The returned exact support table decides whether \(H_{\mathrm{slice}}(S,\ell)\) has positive mass.  Hence, by Definition~\(\mathrm{Measured\ source\ slice}\) and the positive-source-law assumption, precisely the well-typed positive slices that can occur in an accepted certificate survive.  Apply to each surviving slice the same ancestral-set transformation and bidirected-district decomposition used by the complete run.  There are at most \(n\) districts, hence at most \(n\) canonical single-district source factors \(T\) for this slice.  The measured-ancestry assumption and Definition~\(\mathrm{Measured\ source\ slice}\) decide and remove every source whose required transformed ancestors are neither READ nor fixed by a recorded action.  Every test so far is therefore both necessary for acceptance and exhaustive over protocol--slice--source triples that acceptance can use.

Fix a surviving triple \((S,\ell,T)\) and a target factor \(C_j\).  Enumerate the finite branch set \(\Omega_j\).  If the free request positions have domain sizes \(q_1,\ldots,q_r\), then the equality type is induced by the assignment and creates no independent choice.  Moreover,
\[
 |\Omega_j|=\prod_{h=1}^{r}q_h
 \leq \prod_{h=1}^{r}2^{q_h}
 =2^{\sum_{h=1}^{r}q_h}
 \leq 2^L.                                                    \tag{1}
\]
The first inequality uses \(q_h\leq 2^{q_h}\) for positive integers, and the last uses the fact that the canonical literal table has one distinct request literal for every allowed value at every such position.  For each branch, instantiate its value comparisons, construct \(D_T\) from Definition~\(\mathrm{Value\mbox{-}matching\ dependency\ graph}\), and run the deterministic ancestor--district recursion of the published IDENTIFY\({}^{+}\) recursion lemma.  On its stated connected, once-occurring factor inputs, Proposition~\(\mathrm{Connected\mbox{-}ancestor\ obstruction}\) equivalently declares failure exactly when \(\mathfrak O(T,C_j)\) is nonempty.  On success, Lemma~\(\mathrm{Fixed\ transcript\ size}\) supplies the canonical restriction trace, with at most \(|T|\leq n\) strict restrictions and \(O(n^2)\) bits apart from literal identifiers.  Its sets, districts, and value matches are checked by graph traversal and table comparison.

Replace the concrete values in each successful trace by their canonical request-position identifiers and compare the resulting finite strings.  By Definition~\(\mathrm{Uniform\ acquisition\ certificate}\), the triple admits a uniform transcript schema for \(C_j\) exactly when these canonical strings agree and the resulting schema verifies after substitution on every branch in \(\Omega_j\).  This is an exact finite test: necessity is the cross-branch verification clause in the definition, while sufficiency follows by substituting each enumerated branch into the common schema.  Let \(\mathcal W(S)\) be the resulting finite set of pairs consisting of a candidate record base \((\ell,T)\) and the set of factors for which that base has a verified uniform schema.  The construction is exhaustive; in particular, it does not interchange a pointwise existential source choice with the universal branch quantifier.

Form the finite local record universe \(\mathcal D(S)\).  For every \((\ell,T)\in\mathcal W(S)\) and every subset \(J\), possibly empty, of the factors certified by that base, \(\mathcal D(S)\) contains the canonical record with ownership mask \(J\) and the corresponding canonical transcripts.  Include also every syntactically permitted paid-protocol marker from Definition~\(\mathrm{Distinct\mbox{-}protocol\ cost}\).  Since \(k\leq L\),
\[
 |\mathcal D(S)|\leq (1+n2^L)2^k=2^{O(L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}).    \tag{2}
\]
Here \(k\leq L\) holds because each nonempty factor \(C_j\) contains a requested variable-value occurrence, giving at least one request literal with first coordinate \(j\), and different first coordinates index distinct literals.  Every record that can pass \(\operatorname{Acc}\) occurs in exactly one of these finite universes: its protocol, literal mask, extracted source mask, ownership mask, and verified canonical transcripts have all been enumerated.  Conversely, every enumerated record satisfies the corresponding record-local checks.  Define
\[
 w(S)=\sum_{a\in S}c(a),\qquad
 K(S)=\{j\in[k]:\text{some record in }\mathcal D(S)\text{ owns }j\}.             \tag{3}
\]
We next prove the central equivalence
\[
 \exists E\;\operatorname{Acc}(Q,E;G)=1
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \exists\mathcal P\subseteq\Pi\quad
 \bigcup_{S\in\mathcal P}K(S)=[k].                             \tag{4}
\]
For the forward implication, every nonempty record of an accepted \(E\) passes the protocol, support, source-extraction, measured-ancestry, and cross-branch transcript checks in Definition~\(\mathrm{Operational\ acceptance}\).  Its owned \(j\) was therefore enumerated into \(K(S)\), and the ownership masks partition \([k]\); taking the distinct represented protocols proves the right-hand side.  Conversely, suppose the right-hand side holds.  Assign each \(j\) to the first protocol in \(\mathcal P\) that contains it in \(K(S)\), use the enumerated witness record for that factor, merge factors having the same record base, and sort the records lexicographically.  The resulting ownership masks partition \([k]\).  Every record passes the already checked legality, exact positive-support, source-extraction, measured-ancestry, and uniform transcript conditions.  The constructed full source list consequently presents a successful source to the exhaustive complete CTFIDU\({}^{+}\) search for every target factor, so that run does not return \(\operatorname{FAIL}\).  All clauses of Definition~\(\mathrm{Operational\ acceptance}\) hold, proving the reverse implication.

Because costs are nonnegative binary rationals by the binary-rational-cost assumption, a minimum exists whenever the finite feasible family in (4) is nonempty.  Definition~\(\mathrm{Distinct\mbox{-}protocol\ cost}\) charges each represented protocol exactly once, independently of how many of its slices or records are used.  Thus (4) and Definition~\(\mathrm{Optimal\ acquisition\ cost}\) give the derived identity
\[
 \operatorname{Opt}
 =\min_{\mathcal P\subseteq\Pi:\,\bigcup_{S\in\mathcal P}K(S)=[k]}
       \sum_{S\in\mathcal P}w(S),                              \tag{5}
\]
where the minimum over the empty family is \(+\infty\).  Equation (5) is a consequence of acceptance and the cost definition, not a definition of the causal query or of identification.

List the candidate protocols as \(S_1,\ldots,S_p\), where \(p\leq2^m\).  For \(U\subseteq[k]\), set \(D_0(\varnothing)=0\), set \(D_0(U)=+\infty\) for nonempty \(U\), and use
\[
 D_i(U)=\min\left\{D_{i-1}(U),\ D_{i-1}(U\setminus K(S_i))+w(S_i)\right\}.       \tag{6}
\]
Induction on \(i\) proves that \(D_i(U)\) is the minimum cost of a subset of \(S_1,\ldots,S_i\) whose \(K\)-sets cover \(U\).  Indeed, an optimum either omits \(S_i\), giving the first term, or includes it, after which only \(U\setminus K(S_i)\) remains to be covered by earlier protocols, giving the second.  Thus \(D_p([k])\) equals (5).  If this state is infinite, (4) proves \(\operatorname{Opt}=+\infty\), which is the promised infeasibility certificate.

When \(D_p([k])<+\infty\), recover the lexicographically first certificate by a finite self-reduction.  Let \(\mathcal D=\bigcup_i\mathcal D(S_i)\), ordered by the certificate encoding.  Its size is at most \(2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}})\) by (2).  For any prescribed encoding prefix, decide whether it has an accepted completion of cost \(D_p([k])\) as follows.  The prefix forces some records, excludes every earlier incompatible record, fixes a set of already owned factors, and fixes the protocols already charged.  Reject it immediately if forced nonempty ownership masks intersect or a forced record fails its previously checked local conditions.  For each protocol, scan its remaining allowed records with the subset recurrence
\[
 A_{r+1}=A_r\cup\{U\cup J:U\in A_r,\ U\cap J=\varnothing\},                   \tag{7}
\]
where \(J\) is the next record's ownership mask and \(A_0=\{\varnothing\}\).  This computes exactly the ownership sets achievable by a locally valid subcollection: induction on the scanned records separates omission from inclusion, and the disjointness condition is precisely the ownership-partition requirement.  A second dynamic program over protocols and masks combines one achievable ownership set per protocol; it adds \(w(S)\) exactly when the protocol has not already been charged by a forced record.  Therefore the minimum returned by this constrained program is exactly the least cost of an accepted completion of the prefix.  Since (5) is the global minimum, such a completion of optimum cost exists exactly when the constrained minimum equals \(D_p([k])\).

Starting with the empty prefix, try the next encoding bit in lexicographic order and retain the first value passing this completion test, treating the self-delimiting end marker in the same way.  The invariant that the retained prefix has an optimum completion holds initially and is preserved by construction.  Finiteness of \(\mathcal D\) and of every record encoding makes the procedure terminate; at termination its output is accepted and has cost \(D_p([k])\).  If a lexicographically earlier optimum existed, its first differing bit would have passed the completion test and would have been chosen, a contradiction.  Hence the output is the lexicographically first optimum certificate, including the correct choice among any zero-cost, empty-ownership records.

It remains to bound resources.  Candidate generation performs at most
\[
 2^m\,2^L\,n k\,2^L
 =2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}})                 \tag{8}
\]
branch checks.  Recurrence (6) has \(p2^k\) updates.  Each constrained completion test uses at most \(|\mathcal D|2^k\) local updates and \(p3^k\) protocol-mask transitions; the bitwise self-reduction makes only a polynomial number in \(|\mathcal D|\) and the maximum record length of such tests.  By (2) and \(k\leq L\), all these quantities are \(2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})\).  Exact addition and comparison of the input binary-rational costs have polynomial bit complexity per transition.  Every oracle payload inspected is counted in \(N_{\mathcal O}\); caching all replies uses \(O(N_{\mathcal O})\) bits.  Candidate masks, transcripts, predecessor data, and two dynamic-program layers use at most \(2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})\) bits.  Equations (1)--(8) therefore establish the stated query, time, and oracle-answer-space bounds.  The construction optimizes the explicitly restricted uniform-certificate acceptance predicate only; it neither outputs a scalar identifying functional nor asserts a subexponential oracle lower bound.
